items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: make this date with Lee Morlin and Horace Silver and Billy and myself

ctx.x: that; I was just having fun, you know. Oh, I had beautiful jobs, beautiful gigs.

And I was ... like I say, I was kind of established now, recording with everybody during this period, and one day Philly Joe Billy Joe grabbed me one day and said, "Man, come over here to the Blue Note, and make this date with Lee Morlin and Horace Silver and Billy and myself -- it was Lee's first date day, I believe, doin' it, and we did -- called Lee Morlin, and I was fearful because I'm thinking of all this music that Lee got -- and he said, "Man, there ain't nothing to that," and I said, "Yeah, man, come on,"…

But they were teaching me like I never studied. But we got through that beautifully, and Alfred Lyon was very enthused -- he started calling me on quite a few record dates, and I got some calls from Herbie Irving Mann and a whole lot of people, different ones, but they had to get permission from in order to use me, and they signed me up with some options. Oh, but that was part of that New York scene.
